A pump starts and a dye streak changes s: A pump starts and a dye streak changes shape over time. Can a single photographed streak be treated as a permanent streamline map?
The startup flow is unsteady, so particl: The startup flow is unsteady, so particle history and instantaneous direction differ.
Compare observations after conditions st: Compare observations after conditions stabilize and identify whether the diagram represents paths, streaks or streamlines.
Use the correct visual model before infe: Use the correct visual model before inferring flow direction or recirculation. A changing dye pattern is not itself proof of a permanent obstruction.
Laminar flow has organized layers domina: Laminar flow has organized layers dominated by viscous effects, while turbulent flow contains fluctuations and mixing. Pipe-flow transition depends on Reynolds number and disturbances. Turbulence usually increases mixing and pressure loss, but it is not equivalent to cavitation or necessarily an equipment fault.
The same pipe carries warm water and the: The same pipe carries warm water and then much more viscous oil at equal mean velocity. Should the same friction model be used automatically?
Higher viscosity lowers Reynolds number: Higher viscosity lowers Reynolds number at the same diameter and speed.
Determine the regime and relative roughn: Determine the regime and relative roughness before selecting a friction correlation.
A regime change can make a water-based p: A regime change can make a water-based pressure-loss estimate unsuitable for oil. Keep fluid temperature with viscosity data, because cooling may alter the regime substantially.
Reynolds number compares inertia with vi: Reynolds number compares inertia with viscous effects. For internal flow it uses the pipe's inside diameter, mean velocity and fluid viscosity at operating temperature. A regime classification helps choose a model; it does not by itself give the pressure drop or indicate whether a pump will cavitate.
Oil flows at 0.5 m/s in a 0.04 m bore wi: Oil flows at 0.5 m/s in a 0.04 m bore with kinematic viscosity 100 cSt.
Re = VD/ν = 0.5 × 0.04 / 0.0001 = 200, i: Re = VD/ν = 0.5 × 0.04 / 0.0001 = 200, indicating laminar pipe flow.
For fully developed laminar flow in a ci: For fully developed laminar flow in a circular pipe, Darcy friction factor is 64/Re = 0.32. Do not use this relation for turbulent flow or confuse Darcy and Fanning factors.
Continuity conserves mass, not necessari: Continuity conserves mass, not necessarily volume. For steady incompressible flow without branches or leaks, AV remains constant. Gas compression or density changes require the mass-flow form ρAV. A smaller bore therefore raises liquid velocity and can increase local losses.
Water flows at 1 m/s in a 100 mm bore be: Water flows at 1 m/s in a 100 mm bore before entering a 50 mm bore. Ignore leakage and density change.
The smaller pipe velocity is 4 m/s; volu: The smaller pipe velocity is 4 m/s; volumetric flow remains approximately 0.00785 m³/s.
Halving diameter quadruples velocity, ra: Halving diameter quadruples velocity, rather than doubling it. Check the resulting pressure loss and erosion limits before reducing a shipboard pipe size.
Darcy–Weisbach expresses straight-pipe h: Darcy–Weisbach expresses straight-pipe head loss as f(L/D)V²/(2g). Use the Darcy friction factor and internal diameter. The velocity-squared term explains why an apparently small flow increase can sharply increase pump demand, although the friction factor may also change with Reynolds number.
Take f = 0.02, L = 50 m, D = 0.10 m and: Take f = 0.02, L = 50 m, D = 0.10 m and V = 2 m/s.
At 4 m/s, keeping f fixed for comparison: At 4 m/s, keeping f fixed for comparison, loss becomes 8.15 m.
The fourfold increase is an approximatio: The fourfold increase is an approximation at constant friction factor. Add fittings, elevation and terminal pressure requirements to obtain total system head.
The Moody diagram relates Darcy friction: The Moody diagram relates Darcy friction factor to Reynolds number and relative roughness ε/D. Absolute roughness alone is insufficient: the same roughness has a larger relative effect in a smaller pipe. Transitional flow also makes a precise single-factor estimate uncertain.
Two pipes have roughness 0.05 mm and bor: Two pipes have roughness 0.05 mm and bores 50 mm and 100 mm. Compare relative roughness.
Locate each ratio with its own Reynolds: Locate each ratio with its own Reynolds number before reading a friction factor.
The smaller pipe has twice the relative: The smaller pipe has twice the relative roughness. Do not copy the same factor from a chart without checking flow regime, units and whether the chart uses Darcy or Fanning convention.
Bends, valves and changes of section cre: Bends, valves and changes of section create local losses that can be represented by K V²/(2g). The reference velocity must match the coefficient's definition. A partly closed valve can dominate a system's loss even when the straight pipe is short.
A set of fittings has total K = 6, refer: A set of fittings has total K = 6, referenced to a pipe velocity of 3 m/s.
Add this to straight-pipe friction and o: Add this to straight-pipe friction and other system requirements using a consistent head datum.
Fittings are not negligible merely becau: Fittings are not negligible merely because their physical length is small. A coefficient for a fully open valve does not describe its throttled condition.
Pipes in series carry the same flow and: Pipes in series carry the same flow and their head losses add. Parallel branches share the same pressure difference between junctions while their flows add. Unequal branch resistance produces unequal flow, so equal pipe connection points do not imply equal cooling to every consumer.
Two parallel cooler branches connect the: Two parallel cooler branches connect the same supply and return. One branch develops a blocked strainer.
At the shared pressure difference, the r: At the shared pressure difference, the restricted branch carries less flow.
Total system flow may remain plausible b: Total system flow may remain plausible because the other branch takes more; measure each branch's temperature and flow evidence.
A normal header reading can hide local s: A normal header reading can hide local starvation. Restore the restriction and balance the branches using the approved arrangement rather than increasing pump pressure indiscriminately.
Pipe sizing balances allowable velocity,: Pipe sizing balances allowable velocity, pressure loss, material compatibility and the pump's operating range. Choosing the smallest pipe that passes the required volume can create excessive friction and poor suction conditions. Inside diameter, not nominal outside size, determines flow area.
A proposed seawater line must carry 0.02: A proposed seawater line must carry 0.020 m³/s at a design velocity of 2 m/s.
Equivalent circular bore is sqrt(4A/π) =: Equivalent circular bore is sqrt(4A/π) = 0.113 m, before selecting an available pipe size and wall thickness.
This first estimate is about 113 mm insi: This first estimate is about 113 mm inside diameter. Verify complete head loss, class requirements, corrosion allowance and suction margins before accepting a specification.
A centrifugal pump adds energy through a: A centrifugal pump adds energy through a rotating impeller and converts part of velocity into pressure in the casing. Its delivered flow depends on the connected system, not solely on rotational speed. Air in the casing can prevent effective pumping because the impeller cannot develop the expected liquid head.
The motor runs at normal speed but disch: The motor runs at normal speed but discharge pressure and flow remain low after maintenance.
Check that the casing is filled and vent: Check that the casing is filled and vented, suction is available and rotation matches the approved direction.
Compare suction and discharge readings b: Compare suction and discharge readings before blaming impeller wear.
A spinning motor does not prove liquid c: A spinning motor does not prove liquid circulation. Follow the priming procedure and avoid prolonged dry running, which can damage seals and bearings.
The operating point is the intersection: The operating point is the intersection of the pump head curve and the system curve. Closing a discharge valve raises system resistance and moves the operating point; it does not increase pump capacity. Operation far from the preferred range may increase vibration, heating and internal recirculation.
A centrifugal pump previously supplied 4: A centrifugal pump previously supplied 40 m³/h. After a valve adjustment, flow falls while discharge pressure rises.
Plot or compare the new system resistanc: Plot or compare the new system resistance with the pump curve.
Confirm valve lineup and differential he: Confirm valve lineup and differential head at comparable speed before assuming the pump has gained performance.
Higher discharge pressure with lower flo: Higher discharge pressure with lower flow can indicate throttling. Evaluate the operating point and maker's permitted flow range rather than using pressure alone as a success measure.
NPSH available represents the inlet liqu: NPSH available represents the inlet liquid's absolute head above its vapor-pressure head after accounting for the installation. NPSH required comes from the pump's test criterion; merely matching it does not guarantee zero cavitation. Temperature, suction losses and tank level can reduce the available margin.
Available NPSH is 5 m and the pump requi: Available NPSH is 5 m and the pump requires 3 m at the chosen flow. A dirty suction strainer adds 2 m loss.
The initial numerical margin is 2 m.
After the restriction, available NPSH fa: After the restriction, available NPSH falls to 3 m, removing that margin at the same assumed flow.
Investigate and restore suction conditio: Investigate and restore suction conditions; do not assume equality is an acceptable operating target. Use the manufacturer's required margin and consider hot-fluid vapor pressure.
A positive-displacement pump moves a nea: A positive-displacement pump moves a nearly fixed volume each cycle. Outlet pressure is imposed by system resistance, so a blocked discharge can rapidly overload the pump or piping. A correctly arranged relief path is essential; it must not be defeated to force more delivery.
A gear pump discharges against a closed: A gear pump discharges against a closed valve. Why is waiting for the motor to stall unsafe?
The displaced liquid has nowhere to go,: The displaced liquid has nowhere to go, causing a rapid pressure rise.
The relief device should limit pressure: The relief device should limit pressure by routing flow to its designed destination, but prolonged recirculation can heat the liquid.
Stop and correct the lineup using the ap: Stop and correct the lineup using the approved procedure. A relief valve is protection against abnormal pressure, not a normal method for controlling continuous pump output.
Select a pump for the required duty poin: Select a pump for the required duty point and operating range, not maximum advertised flow. Include static lift, pressure at the destination, piping losses, fluid properties and suction margin. Efficiency at the intended duty affects both energy use and heat generation.
A system needs 25 m³/h with 8 m static l: A system needs 25 m³/h with 8 m static lift and 12 m friction and fitting loss.
Required head at that flow is 20 m, plus: Required head at that flow is 20 m, plus any separate terminal pressure requirement.
Compare suitable pump curves, efficiency: Compare suitable pump curves, efficiency, NPSH and minimum-flow restrictions at 25 m³/h.
A pump rated for 25 m³/h at zero head ma: A pump rated for 25 m³/h at zero head may not meet this duty. Verify the complete curve and installation conditions before selection.
In series, pumps add head at the same fl: In series, pumps add head at the same flow. In parallel, pumps add flow at the same head. The actual change depends on the system curve; two identical parallel pumps seldom double the original flow in a friction-dominated system. Check valves prevent unintended reverse flow.
A single pump's duty is 30 m³/h. A secon: A single pump's duty is 30 m³/h. A second identical pump is started in parallel but total flow becomes only 45 m³/h.
Higher total flow increases system resis: Higher total flow increases system resistance, moving both pumps to a new shared head.
Compare the combined curve with the syst: Compare the combined curve with the system curve and verify both pumps contribute forward flow.
The result can be normal, not proof of a: The result can be normal, not proof of a faulty second pump. Check each unit's permitted range and the consequences of stopping one unit.
A ballast system changes tank contents a: A ballast system changes tank contents and therefore draft, trim, heel and hull loading. Valve routing is part of ship stability management, not merely pump operation. The approved ballast-water management arrangement also determines how transferred or discharged water is treated and recorded.
During a planned transfer, the receiving: During a planned transfer, the receiving tank level rises but another tank unexpectedly falls.
Compare the actual valve lineup and tank: Compare the actual valve lineup and tank-level trends with the transfer plan.
Pause the operation safely and establish: Pause the operation safely and establish whether a cross-connection or leaking valve has created an unintended flow path.
Do not continue solely because the recei: Do not continue solely because the receiving tank is filling. Confirm stability, structural limits and the authorized treatment route before resuming the corrected sequence.
Bilge systems collect leakage but also p: Bilge systems collect leakage but also provide clues about its source. A rising bilge can indicate a continuing leak even if the pump keeps pace. Machinery-space oily water must follow the approved retention and treatment route; pump availability does not authorize discharge.
A bilge pump now cycles every five minut: A bilge pump now cycles every five minutes instead of hourly after seawater-system work.
Compare the volume and interval with the: Compare the volume and interval with the earlier baseline and inspect the worked-on system.
Identify and isolate the ingress under t: Identify and isolate the ingress under the emergency or maintenance procedure while monitoring bilge levels.
Treat increased cycling as a fault signa: Treat increased cycling as a fault signal, not successful automatic control. Keep oily water contained and record the incident and corrective action appropriately.
Cooling performance depends on both temp: Cooling performance depends on both temperature difference and flow. A small temperature rise can mean healthy high flow, but it can also occur when little heat reaches the circuit. Conversely, a large rise may reflect inadequate flow at the same load. Use an energy balance with equipment load.
Freshwater flow is 2 kg/s and temperatur: Freshwater flow is 2 kg/s and temperature rises by 8 K through an engine cooler circuit. Use cp = 4.2 kJ/(kg·K).
At the same heat load, halving flow woul: At the same heat load, halving flow would approximately double the temperature rise if other conditions remain comparable.
Trend flow, inlet temperature and load t: Trend flow, inlet temperature and load together. A single outlet temperature cannot establish that every cooled component receives sufficient circulation.
Fuel transfer moves inventory between ta: Fuel transfer moves inventory between tanks; the service system supplies fuel at the engine's required pressure, temperature and cleanliness. Mixing these functions in a fault diagnosis can miss a healthy transfer pump feeding a defective booster or filter arrangement. Tank overflow and return routing must be considered.
A service tank level is adequate, but en: A service tank level is adequate, but engine inlet pressure falls as load increases.
Trace the service route from the tank th: Trace the service route from the tank through valves, strainers, pumps and filters.
Compare pressure before and after restri: Compare pressure before and after restrictions at the same demand; verify the return arrangement.
Adequate stored fuel does not prove adeq: Adequate stored fuel does not prove adequate delivery. Follow the approved response to low fuel pressure rather than changing unrelated transfer-pump settings.
Valve selection depends on whether the d: Valve selection depends on whether the duty is isolation, throttling, non-return or pressure protection. A valve can be mechanically open yet unsuitable for sustained control at a small opening. Directional markings and fail positions matter when tracing a circuit.
A check valve is proposed as the only is: A check valve is proposed as the only isolation before opening a pump for maintenance.
A check valve responds to differential p: A check valve responds to differential pressure and can leak or reopen; it is not a positively secured maintenance boundary.
Identify the specified isolation points,: Identify the specified isolation points, lock them and verify absence of pressure and stored energy.
Use the approved isolation arrangement. Never treat a non-return function as proof that an opened line cannot be pressurized from another connection.
Material choice must address the fluid,: Material choice must address the fluid, temperature, pressure, corrosion mechanism and joining method. Dissimilar metals in an electrolyte can form a galvanic couple. Replacing a short pipe section with a stronger-looking material may move corrosion to an adjacent component.
A seawater repair joins a new noble-meta: A seawater repair joins a new noble-metal fitting directly to a less noble pipe. What additional risk needs review?
The seawater provides an electrical path: The seawater provides an electrical path for galvanic corrosion.
Assess material compatibility, area rati: Assess material compatibility, area ratio and approved isolation measures along with pressure rating.
Strength alone does not establish suitab: Strength alone does not establish suitability. Use the vessel's approved piping specification and class requirements rather than selecting replacements only by thread size or nominal pressure.
A metal's properties depend on its micro: A metal's properties depend on its microstructure as well as chemical composition. A phase diagram describes equilibrium phases; a real heat-treatment cycle also depends on cooling rate and section thickness. Two parts of the same nominal composition can therefore behave differently under load.
A replacement steel pin has the right ch: A replacement steel pin has the right chemical grade but no heat-treatment record. Is composition sufficient evidence of suitability?
Check the required strength, toughness a: Check the required strength, toughness and hardness condition against the material certificate.
A composition match does not establish t: A composition match does not establish the delivered microstructure or mechanical properties.
Accept the part against its complete app: Accept the part against its complete approved specification, including processing and testing. Do not infer service strength solely from an alloy name.
Copper alloys and aluminium alloys offer: Copper alloys and aluminium alloys offer different combinations of corrosion resistance, conductivity, weight and strength. A useful property in one environment does not make an alloy universally suitable. Temper, seawater exposure and contact with other metals can dominate service behavior.
An aluminium bracket is proposed beside: An aluminium bracket is proposed beside a copper-alloy fitting in a wet compartment.
Assess the load and certified alloy cond: Assess the load and certified alloy condition, then examine the galvanic contact and wet exposure.
Confirm an approved method of separating: Confirm an approved method of separating incompatible materials where required.
A lighter replacement may introduce corr: A lighter replacement may introduce corrosion or fatigue problems. Evaluate the entire connection and environment rather than assuming all nonferrous metals resist seawater equally.
Uniform corrosion reduces general thickn: Uniform corrosion reduces general thickness; pitting concentrates penetration into small areas. Galvanic corrosion requires an electrical connection and an electrolyte. Average wall thickness can look acceptable while a deep pit creates a local leak or stress concentration.
A pipe's average thickness loss is small: A pipe's average thickness loss is small, but isolated pits are visible near a support.
Map local minimum thickness and inspect: Map local minimum thickness and inspect the hidden support interface.
Identify the likely corrosion mechanism: Identify the likely corrosion mechanism before selecting coating, drainage or material changes.
Use the applicable acceptance criteria f: Use the applicable acceptance criteria for local damage. An acceptable average reading does not automatically clear the deepest defect or its effect on remaining life.
Heat treatment changes microstructure th: Heat treatment changes microstructure through controlled heating, holding and cooling. Hardening may improve wear resistance while reducing toughness; tempering adjusts that balance. Uncontrolled flame heating during repair can alter a carefully treated part beyond the visibly heated area.
A hardened shaft is locally heated to fr: A hardened shaft is locally heated to free a seized coupling. Why should its condition be reassessed afterward?
The temperature history may change hardn: The temperature history may change hardness and residual stresses.
Review the repair method, affected area: Review the repair method, affected area and required inspection with the maker or competent authority.
Appearance alone cannot confirm restored: Appearance alone cannot confirm restored properties. Use an approved repair and verification process instead of assuming that cooling the shaft returns its original condition.
Marine steel grades specify more than yi: Marine steel grades specify more than yield strength. Toughness at a stated test temperature, weldability, thickness and traceability may be essential to the application. A numerically stronger grade can still be unsuitable for a cold environment or an existing welding procedure.
A repair plate has higher yield strength: A repair plate has higher yield strength than specified but lacks impact-test certification.
Compare the full approved material requi: Compare the full approved material requirements, including toughness, thickness and delivery condition.
Check the welding procedure and traceabi: Check the welding procedure and traceability before accepting a substitution.
Higher strength does not automatically m: Higher strength does not automatically mean safer replacement. Obtain approval for a material substitution against the component's actual service conditions.
Average direct shear stress is force div: Average direct shear stress is force divided by the sheared area. A pin in double shear has two resisting planes, but unequal load distribution, bending and bearing stress can limit the real joint. The simple calculation is a first check rather than a complete connection design.
A 10 mm pin carries 10 kN in ideal doubl: A 10 mm pin carries 10 kN in ideal double shear.
One area is πd²/4 = 78.5 mm²; total shea: One area is πd²/4 = 78.5 mm²; total shear area is 157 mm².
Compare with the specified allowable she: Compare with the specified allowable shear stress, then check bearing, bending, fit and edge distances. Do not use tensile allowable stress directly without the relevant design criterion.
Bending stress varies across a section a: Bending stress varies across a section and reaches its maximum at the outer fibres. The second moment of area strongly affects resistance; depth is especially influential for a rectangular section. A load's position matters because it determines bending moment.
A simply supported 2 m beam carries a 4: A simply supported 2 m beam carries a 4 kN central load. Find the maximum bending moment.
At the centre, Mmax = PL/4 = 4 × 2/4 = 2: At the centre, Mmax = PL/4 = 4 × 2/4 = 2 kN·m.
Use this moment with the actual section': Use this moment with the actual section's I and outer-fibre distance in σ = My/I. Check deflection and support conditions as well as stress before judging a real lifting beam.
A circular shaft under torque develops s: A circular shaft under torque develops shear stress that increases toward the surface. For a solid shaft, τmax = 16T/(πd³). The diameter-cubed relationship makes small diameter reductions significant; keyways and corrosion can introduce additional local stress concentration.
A solid 50 mm shaft transmits 500 N·m. E: A solid 50 mm shaft transmits 500 N·m. Estimate maximum nominal torsional shear stress.
This is the nominal static value for an: This is the nominal static value for an ideal solid section. Include bending, cyclic loads, stress concentrations and the applicable shaft design rules for service assessment.
Von Mises stress combines components for: Von Mises stress combines components for a common ductile-material yield assessment. It does not by itself assess fatigue, brittle fracture or buckling. Use compatible stress components at the same point rather than combining unrelated maximum values from different locations.
At one shaft location, normal stress is: At one shaft location, normal stress is 80 MPa and shear stress is 30 MPa. Assume the simplified combined-loading case.
Compare with the chosen allowable criter: Compare with the chosen allowable criterion, then assess fatigue and local features separately. Passing a static equivalent-stress check does not establish unlimited cyclic life.
A safety factor relates a selected failu: A safety factor relates a selected failure limit to a design demand or allowable stress. The relevant limit may be yield, ultimate strength, buckling or fatigue, so quoting a factor without its basis is ambiguous. Uncertainty and consequences influence the required value.
A component has a specified yield streng: A component has a specified yield strength of 240 MPa and nominal working stress of 80 MPa.
Check whether stress concentration, dyna: Check whether stress concentration, dynamic loading and the governing code are already included in the design demand.
The value three describes this particula: The value three describes this particular static comparison. It does not automatically cover corrosion, fatigue or an unverified material condition.
Propulsion-shaft rules account for torqu: Propulsion-shaft rules account for torque, material and geometric features within a defined scope. A simple torsion equation is useful for understanding trends but cannot replace the applicable class calculation, torsional-vibration assessment or approved drawings. Use the current rule edition for a real design.
A shaft's transmitted torque increases b: A shaft's transmitted torque increases by 33%, with all other assumptions unchanged. What diameter trend does the simple torsion model suggest?
For equal nominal stress in a solid shaf: For equal nominal stress in a solid shaft, d is proportional to the cube root of torque.
The factor is 1.33^(1/3) ≈ 1.10, suggest: The factor is 1.33^(1/3) ≈ 1.10, suggesting about 10% greater diameter.
This is a teaching estimate only. Confir: This is a teaching estimate only. Confirm the applicable IACS/class method, material limits, keyway allowances and vibration requirements before specifying a shaft.
Intermediate shafts transmit torque thro: Intermediate shafts transmit torque through the shaft line; the propeller shaft additionally operates near stern-tube bearings and seals in a demanding environment. Bearing reactions and alignment connect the components mechanically, so a local change can redistribute loads elsewhere.
An intermediate bearing is raised during: An intermediate bearing is raised during alignment work. Can the nearby bearing loads be assumed unchanged?
Changing one support position redistribu: Changing one support position redistributes shaft deflection and reactions.
Compare the approved alignment model and: Compare the approved alignment model and measured bearing loads at the specified vessel condition.
Check the entire affected shaft line. A: Check the entire affected shaft line. A locally improved clearance can overload another bearing, especially when draft or machinery temperature changes.
A hydrodynamic plain bearing relies on r: A hydrodynamic plain bearing relies on relative motion, geometry and lubricant to develop a supporting film. Oil pressure at the supply does not directly prove adequate film thickness at the loaded contact. Low speed, misalignment or contaminated lubricant can reduce separation.
Stern-tube oil supply pressure is normal: Stern-tube oil supply pressure is normal but bearing temperature and vibration rise.
Compare load, speed, lubricant condition: Compare load, speed, lubricant condition and recent alignment or operating changes.
Treat the combination as evidence requir: Treat the combination as evidence requiring the maker's protective response, not as harmless because supply pressure is normal.
A pressure indication describes one part: A pressure indication describes one part of the lubrication system. Protect the bearing and investigate film formation and load distribution before continuing unrestricted operation.
Basic rolling-bearing rating life is a s: Basic rolling-bearing rating life is a statistical fatigue measure under stated load assumptions. It is not a guaranteed replacement interval for each bearing. Lubrication, contamination, installation and misalignment can cause earlier failure even when the calculated rating life is large.
For a ball bearing, the equivalent load: For a ball bearing, the equivalent load doubles while dynamic rating stays fixed. How does the basic rating life change?
Using L10 proportional to (C/P)³, doubli: Using L10 proportional to (C/P)³, doubling P divides calculated life by 2³.
The new basic life is one eighth of the: The new basic life is one eighth of the original value under the model assumptions.
Load estimation strongly affects the res: Load estimation strongly affects the result. Use the correct exponent for the bearing type and assess lubrication and contamination separately.
Alignment establishes acceptable relatio: Alignment establishes acceptable relationships among shafts, couplings and bearing loads. Cold geometric alignment is only one condition; thermal growth and hull deflection alter it. Coupling readings should be interpreted using the specified setup and temperature condition.
A machine aligns well when cold but deve: A machine aligns well when cold but develops coupling vibration after warming up.
Compare predicted thermal growth and the: Compare predicted thermal growth and the manufacturer's cold-offset targets.
Check soft foot, supports and hot-condit: Check soft foot, supports and hot-condition evidence before changing shims.
Do not chase a zero cold offset if the a: Do not chase a zero cold offset if the approved target intentionally compensates for operating growth. Record measurements and verify the full alignment method.
A spur-gear pair trades rotational speed: A spur-gear pair trades rotational speed for torque through its tooth-count ratio. Ideal power is unchanged; real efficiency reduces output. Tooth loading, backlash and lubrication must still be suitable for the transmitted duty.
A 20-tooth pinion at 1200 rpm drives a 6: A 20-tooth pinion at 1200 rpm drives a 60-tooth gear. Input torque is 100 N·m and efficiency is 95%.
The reduction increases torque while low: The reduction increases torque while lowering speed. Verify the gear's rated load and contact condition; the ratio alone says nothing about tooth fatigue capacity.
Helical gears provide progressive tooth: Helical gears provide progressive tooth engagement but produce axial thrust as well as tangential force. Thrust bearings and shaft location are therefore part of the gear design. Smooth running does not mean axial loading is absent.
A reduction gearbox develops abnormal th: A reduction gearbox develops abnormal thrust-bearing temperature after a load increase.
Check gear load, lubricant supply and ax: Check gear load, lubricant supply and axial positioning against the maker's limits.
Review the direction and magnitude of th: Review the direction and magnitude of thrust rather than treating the bearing as a purely radial support.
Investigate the coupled gear-and-bearing: Investigate the coupled gear-and-bearing system. Changing oil viscosity alone may not correct an excessive axial load or alignment problem.
Belt drives depend on friction and tensi: Belt drives depend on friction and tension; chain drives transmit through positive engagement but require correct pitch, alignment and lubrication. Over-tension can overload bearings, while insufficient tension can cause slip or impact. A tight-looking drive is not necessarily correctly adjusted.
A belt slips under load after replacemen: A belt slips under load after replacement. Should tension simply be increased until slipping stops?
Check belt type, pulley condition, align: Check belt type, pulley condition, alignment and the specified tension method.
Contamination or a worn groove may cause: Contamination or a worn groove may cause slip even at excessive tension.
Adjust to the maker's measured specifica: Adjust to the maker's measured specification. Over-tightening can exchange a slipping problem for premature shaft or bearing failure.
A flexible coupling accommodates specifi: A flexible coupling accommodates specified small relative movements and can modify vibration transmission. It does not eliminate the need for alignment. A rigid coupling transfers misalignment forces more directly, while flexible elements can deteriorate through heat, oil exposure or cyclic stress.
A flexible coupling element repeatedly c: A flexible coupling element repeatedly cracks after replacement.
Check alignment, torque transients and e: Check alignment, torque transients and element compatibility rather than assuming each replacement is defective.
Inspect the connected supports and permi: Inspect the connected supports and permitted angular and axial movement.
Recurring element failure can be evidenc: Recurring element failure can be evidence of a system problem. Correct the cause and use the specified element; do not fit a stiffer substitute without engineering approval.
A friction clutch transmits torque throu: A friction clutch transmits torque through contact force and friction. During engagement, slip converts mechanical energy into heat; excessive or prolonged slip can damage surfaces. A hydraulic pressure indication does not alone prove that the full intended clamping force reaches the plates.
A clutch engages slowly and its housing: A clutch engages slowly and its housing temperature rises during repeated manoeuvres.
Compare engagement pressure, timing and: Compare engagement pressure, timing and slip indications with the approved sequence.
Check oil condition and actuator perform: Check oil condition and actuator performance before increasing pressure settings.
Limit operation according to the maker's: Limit operation according to the maker's response and diagnose the cause. Changing a pressure setting without approval can overload the mechanism while leaving damaged friction surfaces unresolved.
An S–N curve relates cyclic stress ampli: An S–N curve relates cyclic stress amplitude to fatigue life under specified test conditions. Mean stress, surface finish, corrosion and notches can change service behavior. Repeated stress below static yield can still initiate and grow a crack.
A shaft never exceeds yield stress but h: A shaft never exceeds yield stress but has millions of alternating bending cycles and a surface notch.
Evaluate cyclic stress at the notch and: Evaluate cyclic stress at the notch and the relevant fatigue data.
Inspect for crack initiation using an ap: Inspect for crack initiation using an appropriate method rather than relying on the static safety factor.
Static strength and fatigue resistance a: Static strength and fatigue resistance answer different questions. Consider the load history and stress concentration when deciding inspection or replacement needs.
A geometric discontinuity concentrates s: A geometric discontinuity concentrates stress locally. A sharp shoulder, keyway or corrosion pit can raise fatigue demand above the nominal stress calculated from the gross section. Improving the transition radius can reduce concentration, but dimensions must remain within the approved design.
A nominal alternating stress is 40 MPa a: A nominal alternating stress is 40 MPa and a simplified fatigue concentration factor is 2.
The local fatigue stress estimate is 2 ×: The local fatigue stress estimate is 2 × 40 = 80 MPa.
Compare with the applicable fatigue crit: Compare with the applicable fatigue criterion, accounting for mean stress, surface and environment.
The nominal section value can conceal th: The nominal section value can conceal the critical location. Do not remove material or alter a fillet without checking the approved geometry and remaining strength.
Torsional vibration is oscillation in sh: Torsional vibration is oscillation in shaft twist superimposed on mean rotation. Excitation can coincide with a natural mode at certain speeds, producing large alternating torque. An approved barred range defines operating restrictions for a specific installation, not a universal speed rule.
The bridge requests prolonged operation: The bridge requests prolonged operation inside a documented barred speed range.
Identify the approved restriction and co: Identify the approved restriction and communicate the unavailable operating range.
Follow the vessel's specified passage an: Follow the vessel's specified passage and manoeuvring instructions rather than improvising a new rpm limit.
Average shaft torque can appear normal w: Average shaft torque can appear normal while alternating stress is excessive. Use the approved vibration assessment and report changes in engine firing or shaft-line configuration.
Axial vibration is motion along the shaf: Axial vibration is motion along the shaft axis. Thrust variations, coupling behavior and structural response can excite it. A radial vibration reading alone may miss the dominant motion, so measurement direction and location are part of a valid diagnosis.
A thrust bearing shows a strong axial vi: A thrust bearing shows a strong axial vibration peak while radial measurements remain modest.
Verify the sensor direction and compare: Verify the sensor direction and compare the peak with shaft speed and known excitation orders.
Check thrust-bearing condition and the a: Check thrust-bearing condition and the approved damping arrangement.
Low radial vibration does not clear an a: Low radial vibration does not clear an axial problem. Trend the correct measurements and investigate the load path before modifying bearings or dampers.
Lateral critical speed occurs when rotat: Lateral critical speed occurs when rotational excitation interacts strongly with a shaft's bending mode. A shaft vibrates strongly over a narrow: A shaft vibrates strongly over a narrow speed band and less strongly above it.
Compare amplitude and phase over a contr: Compare amplitude and phase over a controlled, approved speed assessment.
Check balance, bearing condition and sup: Check balance, bearing condition and support stiffness against the machinery's permitted operating range.
Use an engineering diagnosis before chan: Use an engineering diagnosis before changing operating limits. Do not dwell in a suspected resonance band to gather informal measurements.
Shielded metal arc welding uses a consum: Shielded metal arc welding uses a consumable coated electrode; the coating contributes shielding and slag formation. Electrode storage, preparation and technique affect weld integrity. A neat surface does not establish penetration or freedom from internal defects.
A structural repair is welded with elect: A structural repair is welded with electrodes of uncertain storage history.
Verify the approved welding procedure, e: Verify the approved welding procedure, electrode classification and handling requirements.
Inspect preparation and apply the specif: Inspect preparation and apply the specified examination and acceptance criteria after welding.
Do not accept the repair by appearance a: Do not accept the repair by appearance alone. Hydrogen-related cracking and lack of fusion may require controls and inspection beyond a visual check.
MIG/MAG uses a continuously fed consumab: MIG/MAG uses a continuously fed consumable wire, while TIG uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode with separate filler when needed. Shielding gas and process parameters must suit the material. Wind or contamination can disrupt shielding even with a stable-looking arc.
A deck repair develops porosity using a: A deck repair develops porosity using a gas-shielded process in a breeze.
Check shielding coverage, gas supply, su: Check shielding coverage, gas supply, surface cleanliness and the approved procedure.
Provide suitable environmental protectio: Provide suitable environmental protection before repeating the weld.
Increasing gas flow indiscriminately can: Increasing gas flow indiscriminately can create turbulence rather than solve shielding loss. Correct the cause and inspect the repaired weld to its specified acceptance standard.
A fillet weld's effective throat, rather: A fillet weld's effective throat, rather than its visible leg size alone, determines the simplified resisting area. Load direction, eccentricity and weld-group geometry influence stress. A calculation for direct shear does not cover every bending or fatigue effect.
Two 100 mm fillet welds have 6 mm equal: Two 100 mm fillet welds have 6 mm equal legs and carry a centred 20 kN shear load.
For the ideal 45-degree fillet, throat i: For the ideal 45-degree fillet, throat is 0.707 × 6 = 4.24 mm.
Total throat area is 2 × 100 × 4.24 = 84: Total throat area is 2 × 100 × 4.24 = 848 mm²; average shear is 23.6 MPa.
Compare with the applicable allowable st: Compare with the applicable allowable stress and inspect weld quality. Eccentric load or fatigue requires additional assessment beyond this centred-load example.
Weld defects differ in origin and detect: Weld defects differ in origin and detectability. Porosity, lack of fusion, undercut and cracking do not have interchangeable significance. Inspection method and acceptance criteria must match the material, geometry and service; a successful test only addresses the defect types it can reveal.
A weld passes surface penetrant testing. Can internal lack of fusion be ruled out?
Penetrant testing detects surface-breaki: Penetrant testing detects surface-breaking indications on suitable nonporous surfaces.
Use the specified volumetric method wher: Use the specified volumetric method where internal integrity must be assessed.
A clean penetrant result does not prove: A clean penetrant result does not prove complete internal soundness. Combine examination methods according to the approved inspection plan rather than treating one test as universal.
Nondestructive examination reveals indic: Nondestructive examination reveals indications without intentionally destroying the component, but each method has physical limitations. Magnetic particle testing requires ferromagnetic material; penetrant needs surface access; ultrasonic and radiographic methods depend on geometry and technique. Qualified interpretation distinguishes an indication from an unacceptable defect.
A stainless component is proposed for ma: A stainless component is proposed for magnetic particle inspection without checking its alloy structure.
Determine whether the material is ferrom: Determine whether the material is ferromagnetic and whether the suspected defect is surface or internal.
Select an appropriate qualified method a: Select an appropriate qualified method and acceptance criteria.
A method unsuitable for the material can: A method unsuitable for the material can return a misleading clean result. Document technique, coverage and limitations along with findings.
A bolted joint depends on controlled pre: A bolted joint depends on controlled preload, joint stiffness and the load path. Applied torque is only an indirect estimate of preload and is sensitive to friction and lubrication. Reusing an assumed torque on a differently lubricated fastener can change clamping force substantially.
The same tightening torque is used first: The same tightening torque is used first on dry bolts and then on lubricated bolts.
Lower friction can produce greater prelo: Lower friction can produce greater preload at the same torque.
Check the specified fastener condition,: Check the specified fastener condition, lubricant and tightening procedure before comparing results.
Use the approved torque or tensioning me: Use the approved torque or tensioning method for that exact joint. Higher preload is not automatically safer because bolt yielding or joint damage may result.
A contact sensor needs time and a sound: A contact sensor needs time and a sound thermal path to approach the measured body's temperature. The zeroth law justifies comparing equilibrium temperatures; it does not remove response lag, calibration error or temperature gradients. A sensor touching an insulated pipe surface may therefore disagree with an immersed sensor even when both work correctly.
An immersed thermometer stabilizes at 80: An immersed thermometer stabilizes at 80°C, while a recently attached surface probe reads 65°C. Does this prove a failed probe?
Check elapsed settling time and thermal: Check elapsed settling time and thermal contact before comparing readings.
Compare both instruments against the sam: Compare both instruments against the same stable reference and examine whether they actually measure the same location.
The difference alone cannot diagnose fai: The difference alone cannot diagnose failure. Separate thermal lag and installation effects from calibration error, and never defeat a temperature protection device on this observation alone.
A reversible process is an ideal limitin: A reversible process is an ideal limiting path with no entropy generation. Real friction, mixing and heat transfer across a finite temperature difference make processes irreversible. Energy is conserved in both cases, but the amount available for useful work decreases when irreversibility generates entropy.
Hot water cools through a pipe to the en: Hot water cools through a pipe to the engine room. Would insulating the pipe make an already completed heat transfer reversible?
Heat crossing a finite temperature diffe: Heat crossing a finite temperature difference generates entropy.
Insulation reduces future heat loss; it: Insulation reduces future heat loss; it cannot return the surroundings and water to their earlier states without additional effects.
Reversibility is not simply the ability: Reversibility is not simply the ability to run equipment backwards. Use ideal processes as comparison limits, then identify the physical sources of loss in the real installation.
Exergy measures the maximum useful work: Exergy measures the maximum useful work obtainable as a system approaches equilibrium with a specified environment. Anergy is the energy portion unavailable for that conversion under those conditions. Heat quantity alone does not describe its usefulness: low-temperature heat has less work potential than the same energy supplied at a high temperature.
Compare 100 kJ of heat from reservoirs a: Compare 100 kJ of heat from reservoirs at 400 K and 600 K with surroundings at 300 K.
For ideal reversible conversion, heat ex: For ideal reversible conversion, heat exergy is Q(1 − T₀/T).
The two upper bounds are 25 kJ and 50 kJ: The two upper bounds are 25 kJ and 50 kJ respectively.
Equal heat quantities have different wor: Equal heat quantities have different work potential. These reservoir calculations are ideal bounds; real exhaust recovery must also account for changing temperatures, heat exchanger losses and auxiliary power.
Carnot efficiency is an upper bound for: Carnot efficiency is an upper bound for a heat engine operating between two constant-temperature reservoirs. Temperatures must be absolute. It does not predict the actual efficiency of a diesel engine, whose heat addition, gas temperatures and losses differ from the ideal cycle.
A hypothetical engine receives heat at 6: A hypothetical engine receives heat at 600 K and rejects it at 300 K. Find the maximum efficiency and work from 200 kJ of supplied heat.
Maximum work is 0.50 × 200 = 100 kJ; at: Maximum work is 0.50 × 200 = 100 kJ; at least 100 kJ is rejected in this ideal case.
A claimed 60% efficiency between these r: A claimed 60% efficiency between these reservoirs is impossible. A real engine should fall below the 50% limit; replacing kelvin with Celsius would invalidate the comparison.
Thermal resistances in successive layers: Thermal resistances in successive layers add. In a flat wall, each conductive resistance is L/(kA); cylindrical resistance instead involves the logarithm of the radius ratio. The area changes through a cylinder, so applying one flat-wall area to thick pipe insulation can produce a misleading result.
A flat panel has two layers with resista: A flat panel has two layers with resistances 0.10 and 0.20 K/W. Its boundary temperatures differ by 60 K. Ignore contact and surface resistances.
Total resistance is 0.30 K/W, giving hea: Total resistance is 0.30 K/W, giving heat flow 60/0.30 = 200 W.
Temperature drops are 200 × 0.10 = 20 K: Temperature drops are 200 × 0.10 = 20 K and 200 × 0.20 = 40 K.
The more resistive layer carries the lar: The more resistive layer carries the larger temperature drop, not a different steady heat flow. Include convection and contact resistances before applying this method to an actual insulated pipe.
Newton's cooling relation describes conv: Newton's cooling relation describes convection as Q̇ = hA(Tsurface − Tfluid). The coefficient h depends on the fluid, geometry and flow regime; it is not a material constant. Increasing fluid velocity may raise heat transfer while also increasing pumping power and erosion risk.
A 2 m² surface is 30 K warmer than the f: A 2 m² surface is 30 K warmer than the fluid. Estimate heat transfer for h = 50 W/(m²·K).
Multiply h, area and temperature differe: Multiply h, area and temperature difference: 50 × 2 × 30 = 3000 W.
If fouling or poor flow halves the effec: If fouling or poor flow halves the effective coefficient, the same temperature difference transfers only 1500 W.
A warmer outlet alone does not prove bet: A warmer outlet alone does not prove better cooling. Evaluate flow and heat duty together, and use an appropriate coefficient for the actual operating condition.
Natural convection is driven by density: Natural convection is driven by density differences in a gravitational field; forced convection uses a fan or pump. Losing forced flow does not guarantee enough natural circulation remains. Pipe elevation, restrictions and heat load determine whether buoyancy can sustain meaningful cooling.
A cooling pump trips but the outlet temp: A cooling pump trips but the outlet temperature initially remains normal. Is natural convection now proven adequate?
Stored coolant and metal delay the measu: Stored coolant and metal delay the measured temperature rise.
Check verified circulation and the equip: Check verified circulation and the equipment's approved protection response rather than waiting for temperature to increase.
The initial temperature is a lagging ind: The initial temperature is a lagging indicator. Protect the heat source and restore the approved cooling arrangement; do not infer safe continuous operation from a short period of thermal inertia.
The overall heat transfer coefficient co: The overall heat transfer coefficient combines hot-side convection, wall conduction, cold-side convection and fouling. A thin clean metal wall may contribute little resistance compared with the fluid films. Improving the already least-resistive part can have little effect on total duty.
An exchanger has U = 500 W/(m²·K), area: An exchanger has U = 500 W/(m²·K), area 10 m² and mean temperature difference 20 K. What duty does the simplified model predict?
If fouling lowers U to 350 under the sam: If fouling lowers U to 350 under the same conditions, duty falls to 70 kW.
The loss is 30 kW, but measured temperat: The loss is 30 kW, but measured temperature and flow changes must be considered before attributing a real duty reduction entirely to fouling.
Counterflow keeps a useful temperature d: Counterflow keeps a useful temperature difference along more of the exchanger and can allow the cold outlet to exceed the hot outlet temperature. Parallel flow brings the outlets toward a common temperature. Neither arrangement can transfer heat across a temperature difference that contradicts the assumed local heat-flow direction.
A proposed exchanger cools hot water fro: A proposed exchanger cools hot water from 90°C to 50°C while heating cold water from 20°C to 60°C. Which arrangement is compatible?
Counterflow terminal differences are 90: Counterflow terminal differences are 90 − 60 = 30 K and 50 − 20 = 30 K.
Parallel-flow outlet difference would be: Parallel-flow outlet difference would be 50 − 60 = −10 K, inconsistent with the proposed temperature profiles.
The proposed temperatures are compatible: The proposed temperatures are compatible with counterflow, subject to matching energy balances and adequate area. Outlet temperatures alone do not establish the required exchanger size.
Plate exchangers create narrow alternati: Plate exchangers create narrow alternating passages with high heat transfer area per volume. Deposits can reduce both flow area and heat transfer, while damaged plates or gaskets can permit leakage between fluids. Tightening beyond the specified pack dimension can damage the assembly.
A freshwater cooler shows increasing sea: A freshwater cooler shows increasing seawater-side pressure drop and worsening cooling at comparable load. What evidence distinguishes restriction from a sensor fault?
Compare inlet and outlet pressures using: Compare inlet and outlet pressures using verified instruments and record both flows and temperatures.
A persistent higher differential pressur: A persistent higher differential pressure supports restriction; a fluid contamination test addresses a different failure mode, cross-leakage.
Plan inspection and cleaning using the m: Plan inspection and cleaning using the maker's isolation, plate sequence and tightening instructions. Do not assume every temperature rise requires a new plate pack.
In a shell-and-tube exchanger, one fluid: In a shell-and-tube exchanger, one fluid flows through tubes and the other around them. Baffles guide shell-side flow, but also affect pressure drop. Tube leakage can mix fluids in the direction set by their local pressure difference, which may change when pumps stop.
Cooling water contamination appears afte: Cooling water contamination appears after shutdown although normal running samples are clean. How could a tube leak explain this?
Compare pressures during running and shu: Compare pressures during running and shutdown; their ordering may reverse.
An isolated pressure or leak test can id: An isolated pressure or leak test can identify a damaged boundary without assuming the normal running flow direction persists.
A leak path and a pressure difference to: A leak path and a pressure difference together determine contamination direction. Follow an approved test pressure and isolation procedure; excessive test pressure can damage sound tubes.
Fouling adds thermal resistance, but its: Fouling adds thermal resistance, but its symptoms overlap with low flow, air binding and changed seawater temperature. Compare an exchanger against a clean baseline at similar duty and flow before deciding that cleaning is the remedy. A single outlet temperature is insufficient evidence.
At the same flow and inlet temperatures,: At the same flow and inlet temperatures, a cooler transfers 80 kW instead of its previous 100 kW, and water-side pressure drop has increased.
Estimate heat duty from mass flow, heat: Estimate heat duty from mass flow, heat capacity and measured temperature change.
The combined thermal and hydraulic chang: The combined thermal and hydraulic changes strengthen the restriction hypothesis; verify instrument accuracy and strainers before opening the exchanger.
Record performance again after cleaning. Recovery toward the baseline demonstrates the effect of the intervention; lack of recovery directs investigation toward another cause.
Heat exchanger effectiveness compares ac: Heat exchanger effectiveness compares actual heat transfer with the maximum possible for the inlet temperatures and smaller heat-capacity rate. Hot and cold capacity rates are 4 and 2: Hot and cold capacity rates are 4 and 2 kW/K. Inlet temperatures are 80°C and 20°C; measured duty is 90 kW.
Maximum duty is Cmin(Th,in − Tc,in) = 2: Maximum duty is Cmin(Th,in − Tc,in) = 2 × 60 = 120 kW.
Effectiveness is 90/120 = 0.75. Cold out: Effectiveness is 90/120 = 0.75. Cold outlet temperature is 20 + 90/2 = 65°C.
The effectiveness is 75%, with hot outle: The effectiveness is 75%, with hot outlet 57.5°C. This temperature pattern requires a compatible flow arrangement; energy balance should agree on both sides within measurement uncertainty.
An exhaust economizer transfers exhaust: An exhaust economizer transfers exhaust heat into water or steam. Soot deposits both resist heat transfer and can become combustible. Steam production drops at the same engin: Steam production drops at the same engine load while gas-side pressure drop rises. What should the engineer investigate?
Compare exhaust inlet conditions, feedwa: Compare exhaust inlet conditions, feedwater flow and instrumentation with the clean baseline.
Examine approved soot-cleaning history a: Examine approved soot-cleaning history and restrictions without treating a possible soot fire as an ordinary fouling problem.
Assess cleaning under the maker's proced: Assess cleaning under the maker's procedure and safe operating conditions. Never improvise water application to a hot economizer; distinguish preventive cleaning from the specific fire response.
Waste heat recovery converts part of oth: Waste heat recovery converts part of otherwise rejected energy into useful heating or power. Gross recovered output can overstate the benefit if additional pumps, fans or exhaust backpressure increase fuel use. The useful comparison is the net change at an equivalent ship operating condition.
A recovery unit generates 180 kW while i: A recovery unit generates 180 kW while its new auxiliaries consume 25 kW. What benefit can be claimed from these figures alone?
Subtract auxiliary consumption: prelimin: Subtract auxiliary consumption: preliminary net electrical output is 155 kW.
Check any added engine fuel consumption: Check any added engine fuel consumption or propulsion penalty before converting this into a voyage fuel saving.
155 kW is a subsystem result, not yet a: 155 kW is a subsystem result, not yet a complete ship saving. Include availability, low-load performance and whether recovered heat replaces a real demand.
A steam turbine converts an enthalpy dro: A steam turbine converts an enthalpy drop into shaft work. Available power depends on steam mass flow, inlet state, exhaust pressure and actual turbine efficiency. Supplying a turbine must not compromise essential steam consumers or boiler water level control.
Steam flow is 0.5 kg/s and the ideal ava: Steam flow is 0.5 kg/s and the ideal available enthalpy drop is 400 kJ/kg. Assume turbine efficiency 70% and neglect generator losses.
Actual shaft power is approximately 0.70: Actual shaft power is approximately 0.70 × 200 = 140 kW under these assumptions.
Electrical output will be lower after ge: Electrical output will be lower after generator and auxiliary losses. Verify steam quality and operating limits; a calculated power figure does not establish safe turbine admission conditions.
Cogeneration produces useful heat and po: Cogeneration produces useful heat and power from the same fuel input. Its reported total efficiency depends on counting heat that is actually used. Dumping excess hot water overboard does not create an energy-saving credit, even if the recovery equipment is available.
A plant consumes 1000 kW of fuel energy,: A plant consumes 1000 kW of fuel energy, produces 350 kW electricity and supplies 400 kW of useful heating.
Electrical efficiency is 35%; useful com: Electrical efficiency is 35%; useful combined efficiency is (350 + 400)/1000 = 75%.
If heating demand falls to 100 kW, usefu: If heating demand falls to 100 kW, useful combined efficiency becomes 45%, although electrical output is unchanged.
Compare operation over the real demand p: Compare operation over the real demand profile. Match recovery capacity to consumers and avoid presenting installed heat-recovery capacity as continuous useful output.
An energy balance follows energy into us: An energy balance follows energy into useful output, rejected heat and other losses. Successive conversion efficiencies multiply rather than add. Define the system boundary first so that auxiliaries or electrical losses are not counted twice or silently omitted.
An engine converts 40% of fuel energy to: An engine converts 40% of fuel energy to shaft work and its generator converts 95% of shaft work to electricity. Fuel input is 1000 kW.
Shaft output is 400 kW; generator output: Shaft output is 400 kW; generator output is 400 × 0.95 = 380 kW.
Overall conversion efficiency is 0.40 ×: Overall conversion efficiency is 0.40 × 0.95 = 38%, before external auxiliaries.
The remaining 620 kW leaves through heat: The remaining 620 kW leaves through heat and other losses. A useful loss analysis assigns each stream to the same boundary and operating condition before selecting an improvement.
Heading describes the bow direction; cou: Heading describes the bow direction; course over ground describes displacement over the seabed. Leeway can also separate heading from the through-water velocity, so a current triangle that ignores wind is a simplified model. Compare instruments using the same true or magnetic reference and time interval.
A vessel makes 10 kn north through the w: A vessel makes 10 kn north through the water while a 2 kn current sets east. Assume no leeway. Find the ground track.
Resolve north and east components: 10 kn: Resolve north and east components: 10 kn north and 2 kn east.
The angle east of north is arctan(2/10): The angle east of north is arctan(2/10) = 11.3 degrees; ground speed is sqrt(104) = 10.20 kn.
Heading 000°T produces COG approximately: Heading 000°T produces COG approximately 011°T. To maintain a northward track, steer into the current and recompute the triangle; do not simply substitute COG for heading.
Speed through water measures motion rela: Speed through water measures motion relative to the surrounding water; speed over ground measures motion relative to the seabed. They are vector magnitudes. Subtracting the two scalar readings gives current speed only when the velocities lie on the same line. A cross-current can increase SOG while also creating an unwanted track offset.
The ship maintains 12 kn through water o: The ship maintains 12 kn through water on an eastward heading. Compare a 3 kn following current with a 3 kn current setting north.
With the following current, eastward gro: With the following current, eastward ground speed is 12 + 3 = 15 kn.
With the cross-current, SOG is sqrt(12²: With the cross-current, SOG is sqrt(12² + 3²) = 12.37 kn and COG turns 14.0 degrees north of east.
The same current speed gives different S: The same current speed gives different SOG and track. Use SOG for distance-over-ground estimates, but retain STW and current direction when evaluating propulsion performance or predicting the vessel's path.
Rudder balance describes blade area rela: Rudder balance describes blade area relative to the stock axis. Area ahead of the stock can reduce actuator torque, but forces still depend on speed, angle and inflow.
Two rudders have equal area but differen: Two rudders have equal area but different stock positions. Is their required torque equal?
Compare the force's lever arm about each: Compare the force's lever arm about each stock.
Include actual blade geometry and operat: Include actual blade geometry and operating condition rather than area alone.
The same force can create different torq: The same force can create different torque. A balanced rudder is not force-free; use the approved steering-gear limits.
Electrical power drives hydraulic flow,: Electrical power drives hydraulic flow, which develops rudder torque. Pump operation, pressure and actual movement are separate observations; a running motor does not prove steering response.
The helm command changes but rudder feed: The helm command changes but rudder feedback does not, although a pump runs.
Compare commanded angle, independent loc: Compare commanded angle, independent local indication and actual response.
Follow the steering-failure communicatio: Follow the steering-failure communication and changeover procedure.
Investigate the control and hydraulic pa: Investigate the control and hydraulic paths. Do not interpret normal motor current as proof that the rudder is under control.
The telemotor transmits commands; the st: The telemotor transmits commands; the steering power unit supplies the force. Transmission may be hydraulic or electrical depending on design. Fault isolation separates missing commands from failed execution.
Bridge control fails but approved local: Bridge control fails but approved local control moves the rudder.
Check the remote command and feedback pa: Check the remote command and feedback paths.
Maintain bridge-to-local communication a: Maintain bridge-to-local communication and use the documented changeover arrangement.
Local movement narrows the fault but doe: Local movement narrows the fault but does not clear the complete steering system. Test the restored command chain before normal operation.
A steering test verifies actual function: A steering test verifies actual functions, indications, communication and alternatives. A checklist signature or moving display alone cannot establish correct mechanical response.
The bridge indicator moves, but nobody v: The bridge indicator moves, but nobody verifies local rudder position.
Compare command, bridge feedback and ind: Compare command, bridge feedback and independent local evidence.
Test the required alarms and alternative: Test the required alarms and alternative arrangements using the vessel's approved procedure.
Record observed performance and defects. A feedback or linkage fault can remain hidden if the test checks only the display.
Backup steering depends on available pow: Backup steering depends on available power, controls and an understood changeover method. Shared components can disable two nominally separate systems, so counting pumps does not prove independence.
Both pumps rely on one failed control-po: Both pumps rely on one failed control-power component.
Trace the common dependency and identify: Trace the common dependency and identify the approved alternative control mode.
Use the vessel's steering emergency proc: Use the vessel's steering emergency procedure. Include common power and control failures in drills and maintenance reviews, rather than testing only individual pump starts.
Fixed pitch describes blade geometry, no: Fixed pitch describes blade geometry, not constant thrust. Thrust and shaft load depend on rpm, inflow, vessel condition and sea state. Reversal uses the installation's reversing arrangement. Geometric pitch describes theoretical advance per revolution without slip. Actual advance depends on the water flow and operating condition, so pitch multiplied by rpm is not a reliable measured ship speed.
Usual shaft rpm produces less ship speed: Usual shaft rpm produces less ship speed in heavier weather.
Compare draft, environmental conditions: Compare draft, environmental conditions and shaft power.
Assess engine loading rather than assumi: Assess engine loading rather than assuming constant rpm means constant demand.
The engine may carry more load at the sa: The engine may carry more load at the same speed. Use power and operating limits alongside vessel speed when evaluating propulsion performance.
Controllable pitch changes blade angle w: Controllable pitch changes blade angle while the shaft may keep rotating in one direction. Commanded pitch, feedback and actual blade position are distinct; zero indication need not prove zero thrust.
Pitch is commanded to zero but thrust re: Pitch is commanded to zero but thrust remains.
Check feedback and the approved calibrat: Check feedback and the approved calibration and control arrangement.
Communicate the discrepancy and follow t: Communicate the discrepancy and follow the propulsion-control response.
Do not rely on the command alone for man: Do not rely on the command alone for manoeuvring or personnel safety. Verify actual behavior through the installation's approved test procedure.
Propeller efficiency relates thrust powe: Propeller efficiency relates thrust power to shaft power. Cavitation begins when local pressure becomes low enough for vapor cavities to form; collapse can produce noise, vibration and erosion.
Vibration increases at one combination o: Vibration increases at one combination of rpm and loading.
Compare operating conditions, hull state: Compare operating conditions, hull state and inspection evidence.
Distinguish possible cavitation from imb: Distinguish possible cavitation from imbalance and bearing faults.
Use the approved response and investigat: Use the approved response and investigate the cause. Increasing rpm to recover speed can worsen an unfavorable cavitation condition.
Stern-tube seals control fluid exchange: Stern-tube seals control fluid exchange while bearings support the shaft. Pressure relationships, including effects of draft, influence leakage direction. An oil-level rise can indicate water entering rather than extra oil.
Oil level rises and a sample contains wa: Oil level rises and a sample contains water.
Verify the reading and sample, then comp: Verify the reading and sample, then compare seal pressures and draft.
Assess bearing lubrication and follow th: Assess bearing lubrication and follow the maker's contamination response.
Investigate ingress and protect the bear: Investigate ingress and protect the bearings. Normal oil-supply pressure alone does not establish that the lubricant remains suitable.
Intermediate bearings mainly support rad: Intermediate bearings mainly support radial loads; the thrust bearing transfers axial propeller force into the hull. Monitoring only radial vibration can miss an axial problem.
Thrust-bearing temperature rises while i: Thrust-bearing temperature rises while intermediate bearings remain stable.
Compare axial load, lubrication and rele: Compare axial load, lubrication and relevant operating changes.
Inspect the thrust load path and its ins: Inspect the thrust load path and its instruments separately.
Healthy intermediate bearings do not cle: Healthy intermediate bearings do not clear the thrust bearing. Apply its specific protection limits and investigate the affected component before unrestricted operation.
The windlass handles anchor and cable th: The windlass handles anchor and cable through its wildcat, drive and brake. Environmental loads must be managed through the approved anchoring arrangement; motor torque is not a substitute for a sound brake.
The drive continuously holds a heavily l: The drive continuously holds a heavily loaded cable while brake condition is uncertain.
Assess the operation with the responsibl: Assess the operation with the responsible officers.
Verify the designed load-holding arrange: Verify the designed load-holding arrangement and keep personnel clear.
Use the approved anchoring procedure and: Use the approved anchoring procedure and vessel handling to control the situation. Do not improvise a load-holding method around defective equipment.
A crane's allowable load changes with ra: A crane's allowable load changes with radius and configuration. Vessel motion, heel and lifting accessories also matter. The least-rated component can govern the lift.
A crane rated for 10 t at short radius m: A crane rated for 10 t at short radius must lift at greater outreach.
Read the chart at the actual radius and: Read the chart at the actual radius and configuration.
Include rigging mass and the vessel's ap: Include rigging mass and the vessel's approved operating conditions.
Do not carry short-radius capacity to fu: Do not carry short-radius capacity to full outreach. Confirm the full lift plan, equipment limits and communication before moving the load.
Automatic-tension winches respond to lin: Automatic-tension winches respond to line load but can redistribute forces across the mooring arrangement. Their use must suit the vessel, berth and line plan; automatic mode is not universally preferable.
One winch pays out while adjacent lines: One winch pays out while adjacent lines take greater load.
Assess the operating mode and berth proc: Assess the operating mode and berth procedure.
Monitor the whole mooring arrangement an: Monitor the whole mooring arrangement and exclude personnel from loaded-line danger zones.
Use the approved mooring plan. Consider: Use the approved mooring plan. Consider how each winch action affects other lines, rather than optimizing one line in isolation.
Weathertight hatch closure depends on se: Weathertight hatch closure depends on seals, compression, drains and securing. A closed-position switch confirms only one part of that boundary; debris or misalignment can still create a leak path.
A hatch indicates closed but leaks durin: A hatch indicates closed but leaks during an approved test.
Inspect sealing interfaces, drainage and: Inspect sealing interfaces, drainage and securing points.
Distinguish damaged rubber from inadequa: Distinguish damaged rubber from inadequate compression or structural misalignment.
Repair the actual cause and repeat verif: Repair the actual cause and repeat verification. Replacing a seal alone may not correct a closure or alignment defect.
Ramps and lifts contain moving loads and: Ramps and lifts contain moving loads and stored hydraulic energy. Hydraulic pressure alone is not a safe support for maintenance beneath a raised structure.
An underside inspection is requested whi: An underside inspection is requested while a ramp is raised.
Use its designed mechanical supports and: Use its designed mechanical supports and approved isolation procedure.
Verify stored-energy control and exclusi: Verify stored-energy control and exclusion zones before access.
Never rely solely on a valve or gauge to: Never rely solely on a valve or gauge to hold the structure. A hose or valve failure can permit sudden movement even after the pump stops.
Hydraulic pumps supply flow; resistance: Hydraulic pumps supply flow; resistance creates pressure. A variable-displacement pump may reduce delivery at its pressure setting, so high pressure does not necessarily indicate useful actuator work.
Pressure reaches its setting but the act: Pressure reaches its setting but the actuator moves slowly.
Compare delivered flow, command, leakage: Compare delivered flow, command, leakage and load.
Check whether normal destroking or an un: Check whether normal destroking or an unintended flow path explains the behavior.
Pressure and flow answer different diagn: Pressure and flow answer different diagnostic questions. Do not raise the pressure setting before establishing why the required movement is missing.
Cylinder force depends on pressure and e: Cylinder force depends on pressure and effective piston area. The rod reduces one side's area, so equal pressure produces different extension and retraction forces. Friction reduces ideal values.
Piston area is 50 cm², rod area 10 cm² a: Piston area is 50 cm², rod area 10 cm² and pressure 100 bar.
Extension force is 10 MPa × 0.005 m² = 5: Extension force is 10 MPa × 0.005 m² = 50 kN.
Use the correct working area and load di: Use the correct working area and load direction. Equal pressure does not mean equal force or equal speed in both directions.
Directional valves route flow; pressure-: Directional valves route flow; pressure-control valves regulate or limit pressure. A relief valve is not a positive mechanical lock for a suspended load.

A cooler works but cylinder-jacket tempe: A cooler works but cylinder-jacket temperature remains abnormal.
